title: As Advani enters 100th year, PM Modi praises his political acumen
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
As former Deputy Prime Minister and senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Lal Krishna Advani celebrated his 99th birthday and entered the 100th year of his life on Sunday (November 7, 2026), Prime Minister Narendra Modi said ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness set Mr. Advani apart as a leader. There were very few people whose lives had touched so many different chapters of modern India, Mr. Modi said in an article.

Born on November 8, 1927, Mr. Advani, as a young man in 1947, experienced the pain of leaving behind his familiar world in Sindh, Mr. Modi said. “He rebuilt his life from scratch without bitterness. This trait of being able to build from scratch, against all odds, has stayed with him throughout. It was seen while he was strengthening the Jana Sangh and later building the BJP,” Mr. Modi wrote in the article, titled ‘Bharat Ratna LK Advani Ji at 100!’.

Stating that Mr. Advani had taken up every responsibility with immense diligence, Mr. Modi said that, after working as a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) pracharak in Rajasthan, Mr. Advani went to Delhi, where he worked closely with the late former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Mr. Advani’s tenures as BJP president saw the Congress falling sharply from 400 seats in Parliament to below 200 seats in 1989, and the BJP become the single largest party in Parliament for the first time in 1996. 

Mr. Advani nurtured generations of activists and gave the BJP a “clear foundation rooted in the principle of Nation First”, the Prime Minister said.

“Two qualities always set Advani Ji apart as a leader. First, his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness. This was reflected in his speeches and writings. The Jana Sangh and BJP resolutions he authored remain worth reading even today, while his interviews were consistently incisive and precise. Second, the manner in which he exposed the pseudo-secularism propounded by a large section of the Indian polity for many years,” Mr. Modi said in the article. 

Stating that Mr. Advani had taken up every responsibility with immense diligence, Mr. Modi said that, after working as a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) pracharak in Rajasthan, Mr. Advani went to Delhi, where he worked closely with the late former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. “History shows that it is rare for two towering political leaders to work together for several decades, cooperating with each other without becoming competitors. Advani Ji and Atal Ji set a remarkable example. Together, they changed the course of Indian politics,” Mr. Modi said.

The veteran leader nurtured generations of activists and gave the BJP a ‘clear foundation rooted in the principle of Nation First’, PM Modi said. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

In the 1991 Lok Sabha elections, when Mr. Advani contested from Gandhinagar, Mr. Modi said he had been involved in the campaign. “The people of Gandhinagar sent him to Parliament time and again. As a voter of Gandhinagar, I also had the honour of voting for Advani Ji on numerous occasions. The care and attention he devoted to his constituency is something to learn from,” Mr. Modi said. 

The Emergency was a watershed moment in Mr. Advani’s life, the PM said, adding that the veteran leader had been at the forefront of saving democracy and protecting the Constitution. On Mr. Advani’s contributions as an administrator, Mr. Modi said that as Deputy Prime Minister and one of India’s longest-serving Home Ministers, Mr. Advani had been instrumental in strengthening India’s security apparatus. “His work in improving the lives of our security forces is remembered with great fondness. His unequivocal stand against terrorism ensured India got a tough anti-terror law,” the Prime Minister said. 

Terming the Somnath-Ayodhya Rath Yatra as an iconic moment in Mr. Advani’s life, Mr. Modi said it changed the course of Indian society for the better. “I consider it a privilege that I got the opportunity to be involved in this Yatra from the ideation stage to execution. Being present at Somnath when the Yatra began was particularly special. A Yatra can be very demanding, requiring long hours, constant travel, physical endurance and an ability to remain focused despite fatigue. Advani Ji embodied this endurance,” the PM added. 

Maintaining that Mr. Advani had always shown what probity in public life was about, Mr. Modi said Mr. Advani was also a voracious reader, a big fan of cinema and theatre, and has been an enthusiastic film critic.

title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh visited members of the armed forces at multiple locations in West Bengal on Saturday (November 7, 2026) and highlighted a changing nature of warfare while describing the northeast as India’s “first edge” rather than its “last edge”.

The security landscape around the country has become increasingly complex and the armed forces must maintain the highest level of operational readiness to effectively counter any threats to national security, he told personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force station. Delivering his message on the eve of Deepavali from the key airbase near the frontier with China in the Eastern sector, Mr. Singh, without naming any country, said the adversary now avoids direct confrontation but seeks to exploit certain "vulnerabilities".

He called upon the armed forces to keep special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience, and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats, according to the Defence Ministry. Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma, and other senior officials of the IAF were present on the occasion.

Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important region and a crucial link in India's security framework, Mr. Singh commended the courage and dedication of the defence personnel towards safeguarding national interests. He stated that the Air Force personnel deployed in the region serve as a robust shield for the security of the eastern sector, and their preparedness is fundamental to maintaining stability in the region.

The Defence Minister later reviewed the operational preparedness of the Army’s Trishakti Corps at Sukna, with a focus on infrastructure development along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), deployment of advanced military equipment, and adoption of emerging technologies to enhance combat effectiveness.

Mr. Singh expressed satisfaction with the operational preparedness of the corps and appreciated its contribution to infrastructure development and community welfare initiatives in border areas aimed at strengthening ties with local communities.

Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth, Eastern Army Commander Lt. Gen. VMB Krishnan and Trishakti Corps Commander Lt. Gen. Man Raj Singh Mann were present during the review.

Addressing personnel during a ‘barakhana’ on the eve of Deepawali, Mr. Singh commended their courage, professionalism, and dedication in safeguarding the country’s frontiers under challenging operational conditions.

Highlighting the changing nature of warfare, he said security challenges were no longer confined to conventional exchanges of gunfire and artillery but increasingly involved hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyberattacks, drone incursions, and information warfare.

He cautioned that adversaries were using social media to spread rumours, deploying drones to monitor sensitive locations, and attempting to compromise military systems through cyberattacks. He exhorted personnel to remain vigilant and prepared to tackle emerging threats across all domains.

Describing Sukna as a critical logistics hub for eastern India, Mr. Singh said its geographical sensitivity necessitated round-the-clock operational readiness. He highlighted its importance in the movement of supplies, weapons, food, medical provisions, and personnel to forward locations.

The Defence Minister said budgetary allocations for roads, tunnels, border infrastructure, and modern equipment had been increased as the country progressed towards self-reliance in defence production.

He noted that Indian start-ups and industries were manufacturing drones and anti-drone systems, while the armed forces were increasingly embracing emerging technologies and training in drone operations and cybersecurity.

Mr. Singh also stressed the importance of soldiers’ mental health and emotional well-being, urging them to communicate openly with their colleagues and seek support to deal with stress arising from demanding duties and separation from families.

Mr. Singh expressed gratitude to the families of the personnel for their sacrifices and contributions, and emphasised that while the soldiers remain committed to safeguarding the borders, the nation will always stand by their families and ensure their well-being.

title: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav writes to President, seeks action against DU Professor Sangeet Ragi
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav wrote a letter to President Draupadi Murmu, requesting her to order strict action against Delhi University Professor Sangeet Ragi for allegedly insulting the Yadav community.

Mr. Yadav said that he used the abusive language on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He mentioned that action is necessary so that it serves as an exemplary punishment, ensuring that in a diverse country like India, no one dares to insult any society, class or community in the name of freedom of expression, and thus hurting unity and integrity of the nation.

The three-page letter dated November 6, 2026, was shared with media on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

“I am writing to you in my capacity as a Member of Parliament (Rajyasabha) to express my serious concern regarding the alleged caste-based derogatory remarks made by Professor Sangeet Ragi of the University of Delhi against India’s largest community (Yadav/Ahir) during a televised public debate,” Mr. Yadav stated.

He added, “The controversy surrounding the Professor’s remarks has generated considerable public resentment. According to media reports, the remarks reportedly included the use of expressions such as “gawar” in conjunction with the term “Ahir”. The subsequent controversy has raised serious concerns about the use of caste identity, community genealogy and social stereotypes as instruments of public insult and humiliation.” 

Mr. Yadav asserted that the matter is particularly disturbing because the individual concerned occupies a responsible academic position at one of India’s most prestigious public universities.

He further said a university professor, especially one associated with political science, is expected to uphold constitutional morality, democratic values, social equality and respect for the dignity of every community. 

“A teacher who must be educating his students against societal stereotypes is here himself strengthening unacceptable caste based derogatory stereotypes. Prof. Ragi has been notorious for habitually making indecent and unacceptable remarks and expletives against women folk, dalit community and whole bahujan community from time to time in TV debates,” Mr. Yadav said,

He mentioned that Mr. Ragi’s remarks have caused considerable resentment among members of the affected communities, students and various civil society organisations. 

RJD MP explained that the Yadav/Ahir community has a long and complex social, historical and cultural genealogy adding that its identity, like that of every other community, deserves recognition and respect rather than being subjected to ridicule, social stereotyping or derogatory characterisation.

“No individual or academic authority should be permitted to use historical, sociological or genealogical narratives to demean an entire community or associate its social identity with alleged intellectual or cultural inferiority, “ Mr. Yadav wrote. 

He highlighted that the Yadav community, renowned globally for its valour and patriotism, has consistently made the ultimate sacrifice in the nation’s struggle for independence and has recorded the highest number of martyrdoms in every war fought by India.

He added that the community maintains a distinguished and formidable presence across the Indian Armed Forces, paramilitary forces, and various state police departments.

RJD MP further described that beyond their martial contributions, leaders from the Yadav community have held pivotal national portfolios- serving with distinction as the Lok Sabha Speaker, Union Minister for External Affairs, Railways, Defence, Civil Aviation, Agriculture, development and Irrigation, in addition to governing several states as Chief Ministers or as Governors and Assembly Speakers.

He asserted that among the academic circles there is a growing demand that the PhD theses submitted by Mr. Ragi on various subjects must undergo a comprehensive, de novo re-investigation.

Mr. Yadav said that the scrutiny must meticulously evaluate his research methodology, the veracity of the facts presented, and the authenticity of the sources cited therein.

Mr. Yadav who also works as political advisor to Leader of Opposition in Bihar Legislative Assembly Tejashwi Yadav, pointed out that freedom of expression is an essential democratic right but it cannot be used as an unrestricted licence to humiliate communities or promote social prejudice.

He mentioned that universities must be spaces where differences are debated through reason, evidence and academic rigour rather than through caste-based ridicule or public humiliation. Mr. Yadav also said that the dignity of a community should never become a casualty of political debate or academic authority.

“I request your kind, intervention in your capacity as Visitor of the University of Delhi so that an impartial inquiry is undertaken and appropriate action is considered in accordance with the Constitution, applicable laws and university regulations,” Mr. Yadav said.

title: 42 days of SRFTI protest; classes suspended till December 11
author: Shrabana Chatterjee
content_html:
KOLKATA

The agitation at the Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (SRFTI) continued for 42 days as class suspension was extended till December 11, affecting academic life. Students of the film institute on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that “This Diwali we choose to resist”, while authorities said they were “keen" to resume classes.

“Diwali has always been a special occasion at SRFTI... But this year, the familiar celebrations are overshadowed by fear, uncertainty and an ongoing struggle for justice,” an official post by the SRFTI student union said on Saturday (November 7, 2026), a day before Deepavali. They also said that the day they are served justice will be Deepavali for them.

“While the faculty and administration are ready to resume classes, a section of students continues to remain disengaged from academics and disrupt the functioning of the Institute through repeated violations of its rules and orders,” Registrar Deepak Kumar told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026). He further added that they are asking students to come forward for constructive dialogue.

As of November 7, at least 25 students have received show cause notices, with 11 of them receiving them last Thursday (November 5, 2026). Six students have faced rustication, and one FIR has been registered against student union Vice-President Shubham. 

Shubham is one of the six students who got the rustication notice for allegedly vandalising the Vice-Chancellor Santosh Ajmeera’s office and manhandling him. However, all of these allegations have been denied by the students.

According to the students, two contractual faculty members, and five resource persons of SRFTI have also been terminated from their jobs for showing solidarity with the students.

As the classes remained suspended, the hostels and mess were also closed for students. Many students have been living under a makeshift tent during the protest, as many of them are from States outside West Bengal.

The impasse at the campus started on September 27 after violence broke out on the film institute’s campus as a right-wing RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat (ABGP) held an event on the campus and clashed with students. Several students were left injured in the clashes.

Since then, students have demanded accountability from the authorities for failing to protect them inside their own campus. However, six of them were served a rustication notice two weeks later, on October 15, for manhandling the VC. 

The students are also demanding the VC’s resignation for failing to take action against the violence, which left many students injured. 

Meanwhile, the VC has said in his official statement that authorities have addressed students‘ safety concerns and have taken necessary action and that they have taken disciplinary action against students due to “defacement of premises, provocative writings, intimidation of officials,” and more.

title: Locals burn effigy of Christian priests at Basanti in WB
author: Shiv Sahay Singh
content_html:
A group of locals at Basanti in West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas on Thursday (November 5, 2026) burnt effigy of local Christian priests and submitted a memorandum to the police station against the local priests. Basanti has been on the boil since November 1 after a newly constructed church was vandalised by a mob claiming their allegiance to a Hindutva outfit.

The protest on Thursday (November 5, 2026) was organised by Adivasi Eilya Parishad, a local organisation whose representatives said that Adivasis are being lured for conversion on the promise of curing disease, which should not be allowed.

The West Bengal chapter of National Christian Council (NCC) in a press statement added that effigy of local priests were set on fire at Chowmatha crossing in Basanti.

“Later in the evening, during the Friday prayer service, a group of approximately 20–25 people allegedly surrounded women attending the service. According to the complaints received, the women were forced to break their traditional conch-shell bangles (Shakha) and wipe off their vermilion (Sindoor),” the press statement said.

Father Parimal Kanji, the priest-in-charge at Basanti, stated that the alleged perpetrators were outsiders and not local residents and confirmed that a written complaint had been submitted to the police.

Arpan Rana, State General Secretary of the National Christian Council said that Christian communities in West Bengal do not seek confrontation but justice, equal protection and the rule of law. “The Chief Minister is speaking about religious freedom, yet the practical experience of some minority communities raises serious questions about their safety and protection,” Mr. Rana said.

Herod Mullick, the founding State Secretary of Bangiya Chrisityo Pariseba said that the government and administration’s silence has emboldened attackers, who have shifted from targeting small independent congregations to raiding older, established churches.

“While the police are well aware of the situation and continue to accept written complaints, no legal action is mysteriously being taken against anyone, making the government’s ongoing silence both baffling and suspicious,” he said.

According to Basanti Police Station, an FIR has been registered in connection with the incident of attack on the Church and notices have been issued to some accused.

There has been an increase in attacks on churches and Christian gatherings after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power. According to Christian organisations, U.S.-based research project, India Hate Lab, has documented at least 60 incidents of hate crimes and targeted attacks against Christians in West Bengal across 13 districts between May 13 and September 20 this year.

Earlier this week, a public hearing of survivors of the mob attacks was held in Kolkata where people from several districts participated and shared their experience.
